comparison: Perfect agreement on TaDa methodology validation (C8-C14, C90-C94). Both evaluations find the approach 'elegant and very convincing' with appropriate technical validation, quality control metrics, and biological coherence. Reviewers explicitly praised the TaDa experiments and noted that any unorthodox methodology does not affect main findings.

Complete agreement on neuroendocrine cluster identification (C15-C17, C86). Both evaluations support the integrated computational and experimental approach. Reviewers found the multi-omics data integration 'particularly refreshing' and praised the combined research approach, aligning with OpenEval's assessment of converging evidence.

Full concordance on Spar identification as novel Alk target (C18-C21). Both evaluations strongly support the rigorous filtering strategy integrating multiple datasets. Reviewers explicitly stated the discovery is 'novel' and experiments are 'elegant and very convincing,' matching OpenEval's assessment of convergent evidence from orthogonal approaches.

Agreement on bioinformatic characterization of Spar as neuropeptide precursor (C22-C30). Both evaluations accept the sequence analysis and phylogenetic findings. Reviewers implicitly endorsed this characterization by accepting Spar as a neuropeptide precursor, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of methodologically sound descriptive analysis.

Complete agreement on Spar expression patterns and antibody validation (C31-C37). Both evaluations support the rigorous validation and consistent expression patterns. Reviewers praised the antibody generation as 'lovely' and noted reagents will be useful to the community, aligning with OpenEval's assessment of robust validation with appropriate controls.

Full concordance on Alk regulation of Spar (C38-C44). Both evaluations support the genetic interaction findings. Reviewers found the 'mixed approach presents a convincing argument for a genetic interaction,' consistent with OpenEval's assessment of appropriate quantification and nuanced interpretation of asymmetric gain/loss-of-function effects.

Agreement on mass spectrometry validation of Spar processing (C45-C49). Both evaluations accept the biochemical evidence. Reviewers implicitly endorsed this as part of the overall 'elegant and very convincing' characterization, matching OpenEval's assessment of strong biochemical evidence for canonical neuropeptide processing.

Complete agreement on Spar co-expression with neuropeptide markers (C50-C55). Both evaluations support the systematic documentation across multiple populations and stages. Reviewers accepted this as part of work showing 'attention to detail,' consistent with OpenEval's assessment of well-characterized expression patterns.

Agreement on negative result for gut phenotype (C56). OpenEval notes this as appropriate documentation that Spar does not phenocopy all Alk/Jeb functions. Peer reviewers accepted this as a valid control showing specificity of Spar function, though peer evaluation only addresses C56 while OpenEval also covers C57-C60.

Strong agreement on Spar mutant generation and validation (C57-C60). Both evaluations support the CRISPR-based null allele creation. Reviewers explicitly praised these experiments as 'lovely' and noted reagents will be useful, matching OpenEval's assessment of appropriate orthogonal validation approaches. High overlap (80% Jaccard) with peer R10 addressing C57-C60.

Complete agreement on Spar expression in clock neurons (C61-C65). Both evaluations support the integration of published transcriptomic data with immunostaining validation. Reviewers implicitly accepted this by endorsing the study's use of online resources, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of converging RNA and protein expression data.

Agreement on behavioral phenotypes with acknowledged complexity (C66-C76). Both evaluations support the comprehensive phenotyping with appropriate methodology. Reviewers noted initial concerns about behavioral data analysis were 'satisfactorily addressed,' aligning with OpenEval's assessment of consistent phenotypes across multiple measures while noting some variability and complexity.

Full concordance on circadian phenotypes and clock-specific function (C77-C85). Both evaluations support the robust findings with tissue-specific validation. Reviewers accepted Spar's ability to regulate circadian clock function as novel, matching OpenEval's assessment of well-designed experiments demonstrating clock output modulation rather than core clock disruption.

OpenEval evaluated background literature claims (C1-C7) as accurately representing prior work on Alk function. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not explicitly assess literature review accuracy unless problematic.

Divergent assessments of broad conclusions (C87-C88). OpenEval rated as UNCERTAIN, noting claims extend beyond direct evidence and that 'evolutionarily conserved' relies on citations rather than comparative analysis. In contrast, peer reviewers explicitly endorsed these conclusions as novel and valuable, stating findings have 'potential impact beyond this one Alk downstream effector.' Reviewers accepted broader significance claims that OpenEval found insufficiently supported by direct experimental evidence.
